surfaces.part: vent mound ring with dark hole (ellipse mouth)

answer.evidence: The width profile (rows 6-13: 8,12,14,14,14,14,12,8) is a single ellipse. It is a yellow rim around a dark opening in rows 7-10. The only front thickness is the lower lip in rows 11-13: a bright lip in rows 11-12 and a dark outline in row 13, about 2 rows. That is under 3 rows of vertical face, so the object reads as a flat top-down ring or mound with almost no front face. The 1-pixel wisps in rows 1-5 are steam, which counts as decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny yellow ring around a dark hole, smaller than one 16x16 tile, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged by eye. The outline is tinted (0% neutral dark edge pixels), which matches the references. But the ring has only about 4 steps: a light rim, a mid yellow, a dark olive and the dark hole. It has no grain, clumps, speckle or per-element shading, and only 13 colours in total. The references show 7 and 29 visible tones per tile, with layered leaf clumps and shaded trunk detail. Set next to them it looks thin and flat, like a sticker, with no mineral crust, residue or vapour texture to give it depth. Sparseness alone would not fail it, but the shading is too shallow for a careful artist to accept beside the references.
